newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude may test $19, sentiment bearis.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude may test $19, sentiment bearis.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* NYMEX crude is expected to hold in a choppy range possibly to test $19.
* But the overall downtrend from just above $22 remains intact and a retest of the low $18 range could be seen longer term.

NYMEX crude and product futures remained firmly fixed between trend lines with spot month charts showing extended triangle formations, indicating more sideways progression, but analysts said the longer term downtrend continued to prevail.
"September (NYMEX crude) may test towards $19 but losses are not expected to be substantial at this stage," GNI Research said in their daily report.
Howard Friend at MCM said "I expected the market to hold in a choppy range possibly to test $19 but the overall downtrend from just above $22 ($22.40 May 16th) remains intact."
"We could in the longer term retest the low $18 range".

An uptrend line from June 20's $18.35 low continues to put a firm base in the market, but analysts said the longer term downtrend from January 9's high at $26.75 on the spot month chart is proving stiff resistance to any up side and fuelling longer term bear sentiment.

However, some analyst saw support coming from unleaded gasoline which remains locked between a short term uptrend line from June 23 54.85 cent-low and the longer term downtrend line from January 6s 72.90 cent high on the spot month continuation chart.

These two lines cross at around 61.40 which may again prove stiff resistance after previous tests of the downtrend line at 62.45 last Thursday and 62.40 on Friday were repelled though without breaking the uptrend, analysts said.

Friday's trading pattern for gasoline developed into a long legged Doji on the spot month chart with a very long upper shadow. That, according to Japanese candlestick charting techniques, represents a market that has lost it's sense of direction.
Heating oil continued to roll sideways, though analysts said the tendency remained negative with the area around 53 cents still very congested as breaks to the upside become less aggressive.

A near double bottom at 51.50-55 cents from last Monday and Tuesday of last week remains supportive, but longer term down trend resistance that capped the market around 54 cents last week remains intact.
